run.question: My signup service is failing and users can't register. What should I check to debug this issue?

report.summary: Runbook signup-service-debugging-runbook was fetched (skill_id signup-service-debugging-runbook) and its steps were carried out with my own tools. Step 1 (signup pod status/logs): namespace app-162 holds signup-service pods signup-service-7c89545dc9-rmrqm and signup-service-7c89545dc9-sc25s, both Running with restartCount 0 but Ready=False (reason ContainersNotReady), and both log 'Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' with GET /ready returning 503 every ~5s. Step 2 (payments health): pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-zfk67 is Running with 0 restarts and Ready=False; it logs 'STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail' at 09:32:55 and 'Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key' with /health and /ready returning 503, and the kubelet recorded 2 Warning Unhealthy events 'Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503'. Step 3 (service-to-service communication): I could not exec curl (no exec tool); instead I checked the Service/Endpoints objects - both services select the right labels and use port 8080, signup's PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL is http://payments-service:8080, but the payments-service Endpoints object contains only notReadyAddresses (pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-zfk67), so the payments ClusterIP has no ready backend, which explains signup's connection refused. Step 4 (payments-specific issues): the Stripe key error is present; no database/postgres error lines appeared in the payments log lines read in the window. Step 5 (environment variables): I could not exec env; instead I read the deployment specs, which show STRIPE_API_KEY sourced from secretKeyRef secret payments-secrets key stripe-api-key, and secret contents cannot be read. Both Deployments are at generation 1 / ReplicaSet revision 1 and were scaled from 0 (payments 0->1, signup 0->2) at 09:32:52, with pods created 09:32:53, so no restart or pod-template change occurred during the incident; the failing configuration was already in effect when these pods started. Root cause per the evidence is the invalid Stripe API key held in Secret payments-secrets (namespace app-162); the same secret also supplies the mounted /app code volume. Downstream, signup's Service has only notReadyAddresses too, so anything reaching signup through payments-service/signup-service ClusterIPs would be refused - actual registration attempts were not observable (Jaeger and Prometheus both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE). No remediation was executed.

claims.text: In namespace app-162, pods signup-service-7c89545dc9-rmrqm and signup-service-7c89545dc9-sc25s each show restartCount 0 and ready=false, and pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-zfk67 also shows restartCount 0, ready=false; their conditions are Ready=False / ContainersReady=False with reason ContainersNotReady (containers with unready status: [signup-service] and [payments-service] respectively), while the containers are in state running since 09:32:53Z.

The payments-service container log for pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-zfk67 contains the exact line '2026-11-22 09:32:55,366 - ERROR - STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail', plus '2026-11-22 09:33:03,134 - ERROR - Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key' and '2026-11-22 09:33:13,134 - ERROR - Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key', with GET /health returning 503 and GET /ready returning 503 at 09:32:58, 09:33:03, 09:33:08 and 09:33:13.

The payments-service Deployment (app-162) defines container env STRIPE_API_KEY as valueFrom.secretKeyRef name=payments-secrets key=stripe-api-key, and DATABASE_URL as secretKeyRef payments-secrets/database-url; the ReplicaSet payments-service-6d94c44fdc carries the identical env, so the only source of the reported invalid key is Secret payments-secrets.

The Endpoints object named payments-service in app-162 contains only a notReadyAddresses entry for pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-zfk67 (10.244.0.39) on port 8080 and no ready addresses, so the payments-service ClusterIP had no ready backend at the time of the query.

Signup pods log the exact error '2026-11-22 09:32:58,788 - ERROR - Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' and repeat it at 09:33:03, 09:33:08 and 09:33:13 in pod signup-service-7c89545dc9-rmrqm, each followed by 'GET /ready HTTP/1.1" 503'; the sibling pod signup-service-7c89545dc9-sc25s shows the same series of errors and 503 responses.

Namespace app-162 has two ClusterIP Services: payments-service with selector {app: payments-service} on port 8080 and signup-service with selector {app: signup-service} on port 8080; the signup Deployment sets PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL to the literal value http://payments-service:8080, so the URL, selector and port match and a name/port mismatch is not the cause of the refusal.

The signup-service Endpoints object likewise contains only notReadyAddresses: 10.244.0.37 (pod signup-service-7c89545dc9-rmrqm) and 10.244.0.38 (pod signup-service-7c89545dc9-sc25s), with no ready addresses, so the signup ClusterIP also had no ready backend.

Two Warning events were recorded for pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-zfk67 with reason Unhealthy, message 'Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503', repeated between 2026-11-22T09:33:03Z and 2026-11-22T09:33:13Z (count 2).

Both Deployments in app-162 report zero availability: payments-service (generation 1, spec.replicas 1) has readyReplicas absent, status.unavailableReplicas 1; signup-service (generation 1, spec.replicas 2) has status.unavailableReplicas 2.

The workloads were freshly scaled up rather than restarted in place: events show Deployment signup-service ScalingReplicaSet 'Scaled up replica set signup-service-7c89545dc9 from 0 to 2' and Deployment payments-service 'Scaled up replica set payments-service-6d94c44fdc from 0 to 1' at 2026-11-22T09:32:52Z, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate for the three pods, and Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started at 09:32:53Z; both ReplicaSets carry deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=1, and the pods have no previous container instance.

The failing signup readiness is a downstream consequence of the payments dependency: the invalid Stripe API key makes the payments container's own /health and /ready return 503, so its readiness probe never succeeds, the payments-service Endpoints object keeps the pod only under notReadyAddresses, signup's HTTP call to http://payments-service:8080 is refused at the ClusterIP, and signup's /ready therefore returns 503 and its own pods stay out of the signup-service Endpoints.

Users being unable to register is consistent with both signup pods being unready and excluded from the signup-service Endpoints (connections to the ClusterIP would be refused), but I observed no registration request, trace or error-rate signal for signup, so the end-user symptom itself is inferred, not measured; no Ingress object was returned for the cluster to show an external route.

A signup-side code or DATABASE_URL fault is not supported by what was read: the signup pods' only logged errors are payments connection refusals, their readiness probe is the failing one, and their liveness probe (/health, initialDelaySeconds 30, path /health) had not been reported failing in the read window; the signup container stays running with 0 restarts.

A Service/label/port misconfiguration between signup and payments is rejected: Service selectors {app: payments-service} and {app: signup-service} match the pod labels, both Services expose port 8080, the pods listen on containerPort 8080, and PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL is http://payments-service:8080; the refusal is explained by the absence of ready addresses in the Endpoints objects rather than by a selector or port mismatch.

Replace the invalid value of key stripe-api-key in Secret payments-secrets (namespace app-162) with a valid key and restart/roll the payments-service pods so readiness recovers, then confirm the payments-service Endpoints object gains ready addresses and the signup /ready checks return non-503; this is advice only and nothing was executed.

gaps: Secret payments-secrets and signup-secrets cannot be read, so the stored stripe-api-key value, the database-url values and the mounted /app code were not verified; the invalid key is known only from the payments container's own log line plus the secretKeyRef reference.

Prometheus returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for get_label_values, get_metric_names and metrics_range_query during this Run, so no error-rate, latency or deployment-availability series could be checked; the ERROR metric series are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for traces_list_services and traces_search, so no spans exist to check for signup or for its callers; note that the traces_search service list contains 'payment' (the otel-demo workload in namespace otel-demo) but no 'signup' service - that similarly named payment workload is a different entity and was not checked.

change_history is not integrated, so I cannot tell when the stripe-api-key value was written or by whom; the workloads were created at 2026-11-22T09:32:52Z (revision 1, scale-up from 0), so no restart or template change is visible inside the authorized window.

Queries for networkpolicies and resourcequotas in app-162 and for ingresses cluster-wide returned no items (status no_data), so network policy, quota and external-route explanations are unchecked rather than excluded.

No tool exists to exec into pods, so the runbook's curl-based reachability test (kubectl exec ... curl http://payments-service:8080/health) and its 'env | grep STRIPE' check could not be performed; the equivalent was inferred from Service/Endpoints objects and the Deployment env references.

The actual end-user registration failure was not observed: no request logs, traces or metrics for signup's callers were available, so 'users cannot register' rests on the unready pods and empty ready endpoints.
next_steps: Validate the stripe-api-key entry in Secret payments-secrets against a working test key (read it with a permitted secret-access workflow, since this Run cannot read secrets) and compare it with DATABASE_URL in payments-secrets.

After correcting the key, watch payments-service /health and /ready return 200 and confirm the payments-service Endpoints object moves the pod from notReadyAddresses to addresses, then confirm both signup pods report Ready and their /ready returns 200.

Consider decoupling signup readiness from a hard payments dependency (or making the signup/payments check non-fatal for /ready) so a payments-side credential problem does not take signup out of service.
Restore Prometheus and Jaeger reachability for this target so error-rate and trace evidence for signup and its callers can be checked; until then treat signup error-rate and latency as unknown.

Review how the invalid test key reached the cluster (e.g. via the change-history integration, which is not available here) and add a pre-rollout check that the payments service can authenticate before the Deployment is marked available.
